November 14, 2026

FAA orders third nationwide ground stop in US history after communications failure

tags: politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas, @carolinegleich

The Federal Aviation Administration grounded all departing US flights on November 13 after a communication issue hit every air route traffic control center, citing extraordinary circumstances and safety. Aircraft already airborne were allowed to land, and Homeland Security Secretary Mark Wayne Mullin said there was no indication of a terrorist attack or hack. The stop lasted roughly five hours before being cancelled, with more than 7,800 flights cancelled or delayed by that evening and thousands more the following day. It was only the third nationwide ground stop in US history, after 9/11 and 2023.

Officials give shifting accounts of ground stop while demanding $50 billion from Congress

tags: politics, tech
sources: @aaronparnas, @carolinegleich, @oafnation_actual

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and DHS Secretary Mark Wayne Mullin offered three different explanations within 24 hours: overloaded legacy routers, new security upgrades overwhelming older systems, and a contractor's work on fiber optics and routers. Duffy said he wants $50 billion in emergency funding for the air traffic control system, above the $30 billion the president requested, after Congress had already appropriated $12.5 billion for an overhaul whose first phase is running billions over budget. House Speaker Mike Johnson blamed Democrats for insufficient FAA funding, though Republicans hold the House, Senate and White House. A Washington Examiner reporter said she spoke with 60 air traffic controllers, none of whom accepted the official account, questioning why major system changes would be made on a busy Friday afternoon. Critics noted the administration fired hundreds of FAA support staff in 2025, that the agency was already short hundreds of technicians, and that CISA has lost about a third of its staff.

President remains publicly silent for more than 24 hours after airspace shutdown

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @total.hypocrisy, @oafnation_actual

Donald Trump made no public statement about the nationwide ground stop for more than a day, did not appear at the White House press briefing, and posted on Truth Social about the entertainment industry, Gavin Newsom, the death penalty and his golf course instead. His public schedule listed no events beyond executive time and the standard press pool call time. Officials sent to the podium declined to explain his absence, with Duffy saying he does not run the president's communications. Travellers and commentators criticised the lack of public leadership as over a million people were stranded and cancellations mounted.

Israeli intelligence reportedly warns of Iranian drone plot against Trump and senior officials

tags: politics, defence
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell, @total.hypocrisy

Israel Hayom reported that Mossad passed intelligence to the CIA describing an Iranian plan to use drones to target President Trump and senior White House officials, with senior Israeli and US officials saying the intelligence was corroborated by another Western intelligence agency. Senior officials have been moved to secure facilities and the president's public appearances have been curtailed, with special security measures put in place. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent was recently moved to a military base, and Attorney General Todd Blanche, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Chief of Staff Stephen Miller are also reported to be living on US bases. Mar-a-Lago and the Bedminster golf course have been fitted with anti-missile defences. One account questioned whether the intelligence is being used to build a case for renewed war with Iran.

Cuba says it is preparing to repel possible US military action

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas

Cuba's president said the country is determined to repel any attempt at foreign military aggression and is actively preparing for a possible US military attack. The statement followed televised remarks by Donald Trump saying he would consider a military intervention to free Cuba and wants to get Cuba done before he leaves office. No US military action has been announced.

United States loses measles elimination status

tags: health
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

The United States has lost its measles elimination status after more than 12 months of continuous, uninterrupted local transmission and a historic resurgence of outbreaks. The country had held elimination status for decades. The loss comes under Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.

Producer prices surge 6.5% as top White House economic adviser departs

tags: markets, economy, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

US producer prices rose 6.5% year over year in October, the highest rate since November 2020, with core producer inflation at 5%. Kevin Hassett, a leading public defender of the administration's economic record, is reported to be leaving the White House. The departure adds to a series of exits from the administration's economic team.

Bomb found at Illinois ethanol plant prompts evacuations

tags: legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

A bomb was found at the BioUrja Renewables facility, an ethanol plant in Peoria, Illinois, and has since been rendered safe, according to the Associated Press. Residents within a one-mile radius remain under an evacuation notice while authorities search for additional devices. The Peoria police chief called it a credible threat and said the blast radius had to be taken seriously. The FBI and members of Congress have issued statements, and no injuries have been reported.

Questions raised over FAA AI contract awarded to donor to Duffy relative's campaign

tags: politics, tech
sources: @ericmoutsos

Air Space Intelligence, a Boston-based AI startup, donated to the congressional campaign of 26-year-old Michael Alfonso in March, and in June the Transportation Department awarded the same company a 12-year contract worth up to $875.9 million to build an AI air traffic tool called SMART. Alfonso, who won his seat and is to be sworn in January 3, is the son-in-law of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, who oversees the FAA. The FAA rolled out the SMART software across 22 air traffic centers on November 10, three days before the nationwide ground stop. The company says its software had nothing to do with the outage, and Duffy has blamed 1980s-era copper lines.

US becomes first country to fully skip a UN human rights review

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

The United States is set to become the first country to skip a UN Human Rights Council review of its rights record since the council began work two decades ago. The council rescheduled the review for Tuesday after Washington missed its November 2025 appointment. The Trump administration withdrew from the council in 2025, accusing it of bias against the United States and Israel, and a State Department spokesperson said it gives no credibility to the agency. The council reviews all 193 UN member states on a four- to five-year cycle and says a review requires representatives of the country under scrutiny.

Pentagon renames chief AI office the Super Intelligence Office

tags: tech, defence
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Defense Department has redesignated its Chief Digital and Artificial Intelligence Office as the Super Intelligence Office, according to Breaking Defense. The department said the change does not alter the office's mission, leadership or budget. It follows a September order from President Trump replacing the term artificial intelligence with super intelligence across the federal government.

Washington teachers union sues to block transgender school sports ban

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

Washington's teachers union, the nonprofit TransFamilies and parents of student athletes sued the state to block Initiative 638, which bars transgender girls from competing on girls' school teams, asking King County Superior Court to halt the measure before it takes effect December 3. The plaintiffs argue that requiring girls to verify their sex to play school sports violates their privacy and breaches state antidiscrimination laws and constitutional guarantees of equal rights and equal access to education. The measure passed November 3 with about 56% support, with backers saying it would make competition fair for girls.

Federal judge orders Iowa to let Satanic Temple hold Capitol holiday event

tags: legal, politics
sources: @groundnews

Chief District Judge Stephanie M. Rose ruled that Iowa must grant the Satanic Temple's Iowa chapter a permit for a holiday gathering in the Capitol rotunda, giving the state seven days to approve it. The group sued alleging religious discrimination after officials denied its requests, and Rose concluded it had a strong chance of winning its free speech claim. State officials had argued that Krampus costumes could scare children and that stick props could serve as weapons; Rose said the props could go through standard Capitol security screening. Attorney General Brenna Bird's office said the state plans to appeal.

Saudi court sentences Kenyan domestic worker to 100 lashes

tags: legal
sources: @groundnews

Three Saudi judges sentenced Esther Wanja Muthoni, a 40-year-old Kenyan domestic worker, to 100 lashes in October after convicting her of sex outside of marriage, basing the punishment on their reading of Islamic law. Muthoni had spent more than a year trying to return to Kenya with her one-year-old son, but the case prevented them from leaving. Police detained her for questioning after a supervisor took her and her newborn to a hospital in August 2025, according to court records reviewed by The New York Times.

Marine training center director relieved of command after political speech dispute

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Col. Meador, director of the Tactical Training Exercise Control Group, was relieved of command this week following an incident at a ball where the guest speaker delivered what amounted to a political campaign for himself and was confronted by another officer. The account says the speaker took offense and the commander was removed over the resulting politics. Further details were not available.

Chorus creator network operates as 501(c)(4) with undisclosed donors

tags: media, politics
sources: @total.hypocrisy

Chorus, a creator group registered with the IRS as a 501(c)(4) non-partisan nonprofit advocacy organization, is not legally required to disclose its donors, and a member of its newsroom cohort said publicly they do not know who funds it. The organization says it has close to 200 creators, does not publish a participant list, and asks members to refrain from discussing program details, citing risks of doxing and targeted political attacks. Its launch materials describe funding editors, researchers and bookers and coordinating messaging across platforms. Under IRS rules, 501(c)(4) groups may endorse candidates, run political ads, engage in lobbying that is not their primary activity, fund a PAC and keep donors anonymous.

Connecticut to offer first responders up to $25,000 toward home purchases

tags: politics, economy
sources: @groundnews

Gov. Ned Lamont announced that Connecticut will offer first responders up to $25,000 for down payments and closing costs starting November 16 through a program called First Responders' Time to Own, which has no income cap. Certified firefighters, police officers and emergency medical workers must have lived and worked in the state for two years or more and buy a home where they serve. State emergency services commissioner Ronnell Higgins said Connecticut needs hundreds of police officers and state troopers and has trouble filling its police and fire academies, and a May 2025 comptroller's report found volunteer firefighter ranks had shrunk by more than 62% since 2017.
